data.name: Ashvin
data.gender_notes: Ashvin is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Ashvin are the twin horse-headed gods, the physicians of the gods, and dispellers of diseases. They are also known as the Ashwins, Ashvinska, Ashvinsena, and Ashvinsasana. The name Ashvin carries the meaning “God of Ashvins” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashvin usually hope their child will grow to embody god of ashvins and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Ashvin is derived from the Sanskrit word अश्विन (Ashvin), which means 'Horse'. In Hindu mythology, Ashvin is the name of the twin gods of the constellation of the Ashvins, also known as the 'Dhwajas' or 'Dhanvantaris'. They are the physicians of the gods and are believed to have the power to cure diseases.
